correctness.rationale: The source states \(D=(p-1)(q-1)\) and \(|a_1|=q\gamma_{p-1}+1\). Thus \(q-1\mid D\), \(q\mid m\), and \(p=1+D/(q-1)\). The definition requires \(\gcd(p,q)=1\). If \(m\) is prime, the divisor relation with \(q\ge2\) forces \(q=m\) and hence \(\gamma_{p-1}=1\), after which the degree formula forces \(p\). For \(8_{21}\), \(D=4\) and \(m=3\), so the only forced pair is \((3,3)\), which is inadmissible. The bundled checker verifies the arithmetic mechanism on a finite regression range but is not used as proof.

value.rationale: The source explicitly elevates ordered-parameter uniqueness to a conjecture. The prime-gap theorem proves that conjecture on a naturally recognizable infinite subfamily using only the Alexander polynomial and turns the two source formulas into a finite recognition sieve. The 8_21 application also removes the external-period input used in the source example, showing that the reformulation has practical discriminatory power rather than being only a relabeling of the formulas.
